# Evaluating ∫ -3x²eˣ dx

I'll use **tabular integration by parts**, differentiating the polynomial and integrating the exponential.

## Setup

| Derivatives of -3x² | Integrals of eˣ | Sign |
|---|---|---|
| -3x² | eˣ | + |
| -6x | eˣ | − |
| -6 | eˣ | + |
| 0 | eˣ | − |

## Multiplying along the diagonals:

$$+(-3x^2)(e^x) - (-6x)(e^x) + (-6)(e^x)$$

$$= -3x^2 e^x + 6x e^x - 6e^x$$

## Verification (differentiate the result):

$$\frac{d}{dx}\left[-3x^2 e^x + 6x e^x - 6e^x\right]$$
$$= (-6x - 3x^2)e^x + (6 + 6x)e^x - 6e^x$$
$$= -3x^2 e^x + (-6x + 6x)e^x + (6 - 6)e^x$$
$$= -3x^2 e^x \checkmark$$

## Result

$$\int -3x^2 e^x \, dx = -3x^2 e^x + 6x e^x - 6e^x + C$$

<answer>-3*x**2*exp(x) + 6*x*exp(x) - 6*exp(x) + C</answer>
